theme.name: Circumvention of POTAS through associated entities
theme.claim: Promoters can evade the POTAS regime by reorganising their business to share control of a promoting business or to place a person or persons between themselves and it, so the 2015 associated and successor entity rules do not work as intended.

text.line: Who is likely to be affected Promoters of avoidance schemes who seek to circumvent the Promoters of Tax Avoidance Schemes ( POTAS ) legislation through the use of associated and successor entities.
Background to the measure Changes to the POTAS legislation were introduced in Finance Act ( FA )
2015 to ensure promoters cannot use associated and successor entities to circumvent the legislation.

theme.name: Nature of the POTAS regime and its target
theme.claim: POTAS aims to change the behaviour of a small and persistent minority of promoters through conduct notices and monitoring notices, which depend on the threshold conditions being attributed to the right persons and bodies.

text.line: The POTAS legislation was introduced in FA 2014 and aims to change the behaviour of a small and persistent minority of promoters of tax avoidance schemes who display certain behaviours.
Where any one of a number of conditions are met, HMRC must consider whether to give the promoter a conduct notice lasting for up to two years.
A conduct notice imposes conditions on how that promoter must behave.
If the promoter breaches the conditions of the conduct notice, HMRC may apply to the Tribunal for approval to give the promoter a monitoring notice.
Monitored promoters are subject to additional information requirements and penalties for non-compliance with those requirements.
